title: Spider-Man Swings Back to Theaters
summary: Spider-Man is swinging back into cinemas. Sony is re-releasing Spider-Man: Brand New Day on December 4, with tickets going on sale November 19. The film only left theaters not long ago, but it is already the biggest domestic release of all time, and the studio wants to give it another chance to add to its record box office haul. The new version will be an extended cut, cheekily titled Spider-Man: Brand New Brand New Day, featuring one deleted scene in which Rosario Dawson stars as a character called the Night Nurse. Director Daniel Destin Cretton had previously told reporters that Dawson shot a scene for the film that was cut. The real reason for the return is the box office. The film is only $41 million short of $1 billion in domestic ticket sales, and the studio believes the re-release could push it over the line. For comparison, the re-release of Avengers Endgame: Encore managed to gross $40 million in the United States. Sony also sees the film as an awards contender. Studio chief Tom Rothman recently said the company is launching a campaign for the film and believes Brand New Day is worthy of a Best Picture nomination. He asked whether anyone could really name ten films this year that are better than it. The re-release will also help keep the film in people's minds during awards season, when early-year and summer contenders often return to theaters. The only other new wide release on December 4 is Violent Night 2, so it is a relatively light weekend, although the Christmas box office will be crowded, including Sony's own Jumanji: Open World and Avengers: Doomsday the weekend before. For fans who missed it the first time, or who want to see the extra scene, December 4 is the date to circle.
why_it_matters: Re-releases show how studios try to turn a hit film into a record-breaker and an awards winner.
